title: 7.4 A 112Gb/s DSP-Based PAM-4 Receiver with an LC-Resonator-Based CTLE for >52dB Loss Compensation in 4nm FinFET
problem: High-speed wireline transceivers (100Gb/s+) for AI/GPU interconnects and PCIe 7.0 require signal recovery over long channels with severe channel loss (>52dB). Traditional Continuous-Time Linear Equalization (CTLE) struggles with high-loss channels; existing DSP-based receivers lack energy-efficient, broadband equalization architectures.
motivation: Data-center AI accelerators demand long-reach high-speed interconnects (Ethernet/PCIe 7.0 at 100-128GT/s); conventional CTLE limitations bottleneck transceiver design for extreme loss compensation.
method: DSP-based 112Gb/s PAM-4 receiver with novel LC-resonator-based CTLE providing >52dB loss compensation. Architecture combines: (1) LC-resonator front-end achieving broadband peaking/gain without power-hungry analog inductors; (2) DSP backend for adaptive equalization and PAM-4 symbol detection; (3) latency reduction techniques (analog data path optimization) minimizing overall receive latency. 4nm FinFET implementation achieves energy efficiency suitable for data-center deployment.
key_novelty: LC-resonator-based CTLE enabling >52dB loss compensation in energy-efficient DSP-based PAM-4 receiver.
contributions: Analog data path latency reduction techniques
limitations: Abstract does not provide energy consumption (pJ/bit), die area, clock frequency, eye-width/eye-height metrics, or comparison with state-of-art PCIe 7.0/Ethernet transceivers.
primary_theme: LC-resonator CTLE for energy-efficient extreme-loss PAM-4 reception
